Class EcologicalStoichiometryEngine

java.lang.Object
org.ether.society.core.engine.AbstractSimulationEngine
org.ether.society.engines.tier1.EcologicalStoichiometryEngine
All Implemented Interfaces:
SimulationEngineModule
public class EcologicalStoichiometryEngine extends AbstractSimulationEngine
Ecological Stoichiometry & Biogeochemical Element Allocation Engine.

Formalizes the stoichiometric mass-balance principles established by Sterner & Elser (2002, Ecological Stoichiometry: The Biology of Elements from Molecules to the Biosphere, Princeton University Press) and Alfred Redfield (1934, 1958).

Key Biophysical Mechanics:

  1. Redfield Molar Invariants: Marine phytoplankton \(\text{C:N:P} = 106:16:1\) molar ratio (\(\approx 41.0 : 7.2 : 1.0\) by mass).
  2. Terrestrial Plant & Agronomic Stoichiometry: Foliar and grain tissues maintain tight elemental balances (\(\text{C:N:P} \approx 40.0 : 2.0 : 0.2\) by mass).
  3. Continuous Liebig Multi-Nutrient Limitation: Replaces discrete min-thresholds with smooth (\(C^\infty\)) softmin functions over available N-P-K soil pools.
  4. Elevated \(\text{CO}_2\) Protein Dilution Effect (Loladze 2002, 2014; Myers et al. 2014): Atmospheric carbon saturation accelerates carbohydrate synthesis faster than root nitrogen transpiration, diluting crop protein and mineral density by up to \(\sim 10\text{--}15\%\).

  • Method Details

    • calculateContinuousLiebigFactor

      public static double calculateContinuousLiebigFactor(double nitrogenRatio, double phosphorusRatio, double potassiumRatio)
      Calculates the continuous Liebig multi-nutrient growth limitation factor: \[ L(\text{N}, \text{P}, \text{K}) = \text{softmin}\left(\frac{\text{N}}{\text{N}_{\text{opt}}}, \; \text{softmin}\left(\frac{\text{P}}{\text{P}_{\text{opt}}}, \; \frac{\text{K}}{\text{K}_{\text{opt}}}, \; 10.0\right), \; 10.0\right) \]
      Parameters:
      nitrogenRatio - available N relative to optimal requirement
      phosphorusRatio - available P relative to optimal requirement
      potassiumRatio - available K relative to optimal requirement
      Returns:
      dimensionless yield scalar in \([0, 1]\)

    • calculateProteinDilutionFactor

      public static double calculateProteinDilutionFactor(double co2Ppm)
      Calculates the nutritional protein dilution factor under elevated atmospheric \(\text{CO}_2\) (Loladze 2002, 2014; Myers et al. 2014 Nature): \[ D_{\text{protein}}(\text{CO}_2) = 1.0 - \delta_{\text{max}} \cdot \tanh\left(\frac{\max(0, \text{CO}_2 - 280)}{350.0}\right) \]
      Parameters:
      co2Ppm - atmospheric carbon dioxide concentration in ppm
      Returns:
      nutritional quality multiplier in \([0.88, 1.0]\)
